list: The official 55 trophies, frozen 2026-11-18. Names, descriptions and grades are exactly as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase / PSNProfiles). Guides are written in our own words from the official descriptions; where a place or step is not pinned down by the official description, the guide says so.
sources: Exophase — official trophy names, descriptions and grades: exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
PSNProfiles — grades and PSN progress targets: psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi
PlanetGTA6, OutputLag, KeenGamer and PowerPyx — early-guide reports, labelled reported / not yet confirmed wherever they are used

notes.release: Grand Theft Auto VI released 19 November 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is no PC version at launch.
notes.story_time: Early guides estimate the story at about 60 hours; that figure is an estimate, not yet confirmed.
notes.platinum_time: Early guides estimate the platinum at about 200 hours; that figure is an estimate, not yet confirmed.
notes.cheats: Early guides report that using cheats disables trophies, as in GTA V. Treat that as reported, not yet confirmed.
notes.missables: No confirmed missable list exists yet. Only Positive Mental Attitude is reported as potentially missable (see its entry). Make a manual save at the start of each chapter.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one unlocks automatically. Work through the roadmap in this guide in order: story first, then stranger strands, then activities and collectibles, then robberies and money, and finally the 100% completion cleanup for A Long Road. There is no shortcut — the platinum is the reward for finishing everything else.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end. This is the first story mission, so it unlocks naturally as you start the game. Follow the on-screen objectives; no preparation or side activity is needed first.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. The trophy pops when the chapter ends, so keep playing the main story in order. Before you leave Chapter 1, make a manual save: early guides report that one meditation spot in this chapter may not be repeatable, so a save protects your cleanup later.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one is unmissable as long as you complete the story — it pops at the chapter's end. Make a manual save at the start of the chapter, as a habit, in case any later trophy turns out to be chapter-locked.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. Keep following the main story path and the trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. This is a good point to check your side progress: stranger strands and activities you have passed are worth picking up while you are in the area.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so once it pops you are close to the end of the story. Before the final mission, make a manual save — it is the safest way to protect any trophy you still need from the endgame.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission. It unlocks after Chapter 4, so just keep playing the main story to its conclusion. The mission's name and choices are hidden in this guide until you earn it — turn spoilers off if you want to read them first.

trophies.name: Trust
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in your mission list. It is a story mission, so it cannot be missed by skipping side content — play the main story in order and it will come up. Follow the mission objectives as given in game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heists in GTA VI are story beats, so this one arrives as part of the main plot. Prepare as the mission asks — stock up on ammo and armour before you start, and expect a long, multi-stage job.

trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. It is part of the main story, so play the missions in order and it will unlock when you finish it. No side activity is required beforehand.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. As with the other mission trophies, this one comes from the main story alone. If it has not appeared yet, keep playing story missions — it is not tied to any collectible or activity.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. The name points to the Vice City International Airport, so expect an airport-set mission when it arrives in the story. Finish it and the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. It is a main-story mission, so it unlocks in order as you play. The official description gives no extra conditions, so there is nothing to prepare beyond playing the mission itself.

trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's stats screen. The official list does not publish the exact contents of 100% completion yet, so do not trust any checklist that claims to know it for certain. In practice it means finishing the story, all stranger strands, all activities, collectibles and the other counted tasks in this guide — leave this trophy for last and use the roadmap's cleanup stage to work through what is left.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (250)
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, flips, near-misses and airtime the game counts as you drive and ride around Leonida — the counter is tracked by PlayStation, so you can watch it climb in the trophy's progress. The fastest honest way is to keep a fast bike or car handy and chain jumps off ramps and hills while travelling between missions, rather than grinding one spot. It is a long count, so start early and let it build up over the whole playthrough.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. The official description does not name the 9 types, so use the activities the game itself lists — races, fishing, shooting range, arcade games, bowling, drone races and the other open-world activities all count as types. Open the activities menu in game, work down the list, and try one of each. You do not need to win or finish them, just try them.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (42)
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. There are 42 challenges in total, and every one of them needs gold — silver or bronze does not count. Visit the shooting range, work through the challenges one at a time, and replay any that fall short of gold. Bring your best weapons and take your time aiming: the range rewards accuracy over speed, and you can retry a challenge as often as you like.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (14)
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations. Each location has its own race, and you need a win at every one — winning the same location twice does not help. Learn each course's turns before you race it for real, and use the drone's boost on the straights. The game marks which locations you have won, so work through the list and mop up the ones you missed.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (20)
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different matters: winning the same race 20 times does not count. Try a new race each time — road races, off-road and the other race types the game offers — and pick a fast, well-handling car for each. You can track which races you have won from the race list in game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival you meet through the fishing activity — challenge him and out-fish him in the challenge. Fishing in GTA VI is about timing the reel and keeping the line tension right, so watch the on-screen prompts rather than mashing the button. If you lose, you can challenge him again.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade machine in the world, start any game on it, and play it to its end — you do not need a high score, just a completion. Pick the shortest-looking game if you want this one done quickly, and remember it also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission. Andy is one of the stranger characters whose mission strand runs through the game — follow his missions in order until the strand ends. Stranger strands are easy to leave half-finished, so check your mission list for Andy's icon if you are unsure where you left him.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission. Kenton's strand is another stranger storyline — play his missions in order until the last one is done. The trophy's name hints at a boat, so expect a water-based finale, and keep an eye out for his missions whenever you are near the coast.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission. Billy's strand is a stranger storyline like Andy's and Kenton's — follow it to its end. If his missions stop appearing, check the map for his icon and make sure you have finished any earlier mission of his that is still open.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (8)
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. A strand is a whole storyline for one stranger character — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone are five of them, and there are more to find. Each strand is several missions long, so this trophy takes most of the game to finish. Keep accepting stranger missions whenever their icons appear on the map, and do not leave a strand half-done if you can help it.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. Randy is another stranger character — play his missions in order until the strand closes. Stranger strands often unlock as the story advances, so if Randy's next mission is not available yet, keep playing the main story and come back.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission. Tyrone's strand is one of the stranger storylines — follow it through to its last mission. As with the other stranger trophies, the key is to keep the strand moving: do his missions when they appear rather than leaving them for the endgame.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (18)
PlanetGTA6 / OutputLag / KeenGamer — early-guide report that the Chapter 1 balcony spot may be missable (reported, not yet confirmed)
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places in the world where Lucia can meditate — visit each one and complete the meditation. POTENTIALLY MISSABLE (reported, not yet confirmed): early guides report that the balcony meditation spot in Chapter 1 cannot be revisited, because there is no mission replay for it. Until that is confirmed, treat it as missable: meditate at the balcony spot while you are still in Chapter 1, and make a manual save at the start of every chapter. The other 17 spots are in the open world and can be visited at any time.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a stranger character who asks you to hunt a specific, one-of-a-kind animal — follow his strand until the hunt is offered, then track the animal down. The official description does not name the animal or its location, so follow Bret's instructions and the in-game markers when the hunt begins. A scoped rifle and patience help more than firepower here.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (3)
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida — collect a full set and it counts as one, and you need three complete sets. The official description does not say how many cards are in a set or where they are, so pick up every card you pass and check your collection menu to see which sets are close to complete. Leave this for the cleanup stage, when you can sweep the map systematically.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (100)
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game tag or mark you leave at spots around Leonida — find a WAiNK spot, use it, and move on to the next. There are at least 100 of them, so this is a long exploration trophy: do it alongside the Leonida exploration for The Goodtime State, and tick off each area as you clear it. Your progress is tracked by PlayStation, so you can see the count climb.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (50)
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the small goals the game sets across activities, driving, combat and exploration — open the challenges menu in game and work through the ones that suit how you play. Pick the easiest ones first to build the count quickly, then return for the harder ones during cleanup. You do not need to complete every challenge in the game, just 50 of them.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Build a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the police and escape. Do it with Lucia or Jason as your partner, in a car, away from the story — cause enough trouble to reach four stars, then break line of sight and hide until the stars clear. A fast car, a quiet hiding spot and a bit of patience are all you need; do not try it on foot.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (3)
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level between them. Plan a route past three shops that are close together, rob the first, then drive straight to the next — do not stop, and do not let the wanted level drop to zero before the third robbery. Your partner must be with you for all three. If the level drops, start the chain again.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (100)
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovering means getting into or driving a vehicle type you have not found before — the game tracks which ones you have seen. Drive everything you pass: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and anything else with wheels. Variety matters more than speed, so take a different vehicle each time you travel and the count will climb on its own.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (5)
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode — activate it when five or more enemies are in front of you, then take them down one by one before it ends. The easiest place is a mission or shootout with a group of enemies in the open; wait until they are clustered, trigger Combat Focus, and aim carefully rather than spraying.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the Vice City International Airport. The wording points to leaving the airport in a plane without a scheduled flight — a story moment, so it most likely happens during a mission. Play the story and, when a mission takes you to the airport, follow its objectives; the trophy should pop as part of that mission.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: The description is a joke about the Rhino tank, and the trophy is hidden, so it is tied to a story moment with a tank. Play the main story and, when a mission puts you in or against a Rhino, play it through — the trophy will pop from that mission. Do not try to steal a tank in free roam for this one; the official description gives no free-roam condition.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Go in quietly: move slowly, avoid the staff's line of sight, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. A suppressed weapon and a quick exit help, but the key is patience — if you are spotted, the attempt fails, so reload a save and try a quieter route.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (5)
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets — plan each one, get in, take the money and get out before the police close in. You need five successful escapes, so do not rush: a clean getaway counts, a capture does not. Spread them across the game rather than trying all five in one session.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — find one, stop it, take the cash and get away before the police arrive. A sticky bomb or a heavy vehicle to block it works well, but the escape matters as much as the robbery: have a fast getaway car ready and a hiding spot in mind before you start.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (52)
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The state is divided into 52 named areas, and visiting each one counts toward the trophy — the game tracks which areas you have been to. Drive or fly across the whole map, from Vice City to the far corners of Leonida, and check the map for areas you have not visited yet. Do this alongside the WAiNK and meditation cleanup, since the same trips cover several trophies at once.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (9)
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations — find one for each gang, rob it, and move on to the next gang. The operations are marked in the world once you know what to look for, so learn one gang's operation first, then repeat the pattern for the other eight. Keep a note of which gangs you have done.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a quiet story moment on the beach — a hidden trophy, so it most likely happens during a mission or a cutscene at Ocean Beach. Play the story and, when a mission takes you to the beach, follow it through; the trophy pops from that moment. Do not try to order a cocktail in free roam for this one — the official description gives no free-roam condition.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. This is a hidden story trophy, so it happens during a mission in a showroom — drive out through the glass, in classic GTA style, when the mission asks for it. Play the main story and the moment will come; there is no free-roam showroom trick to do beforehand.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The name and the hidden flag point to a story moment at the bowling alley — play the story mission that takes you there and follow it through. Bowling is also an activity in its own right, so if you want to practise first, a game at the alley counts toward trying an activity type for Master of None.

trophies.name: Personal Best
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — a partnership with mass appeal — and the trophy is hidden, so it comes from a story moment between the two protagonists. Keep playing the main story; the trophy pops when that partnership moment happens. There is nothing to prepare and no side activity tied to it in the official description.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Make a story choice. The description — choices made, for better or worse — points to a decision point in the story where you pick one path. Play the story to that choice, make your pick, and the trophy pops. If you are worried about picking the wrong option, make a manual save before the choice so you can try the other one later.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: The description — second time's the charm — suggests a story moment you have to attempt twice, or a second try at something that failed the first time. It is hidden, so it comes from the story: keep playing, and when a mission or moment repeats, play it through to the end. Do not reload an old save to avoid a failure — the second attempt may be exactly what this trophy wants.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: The description — what the hell just happened? — points to a strange or surprising story moment, the kind GTA hides in plain sight. It is a hidden trophy, so it will pop from a story beat you cannot plan for in advance. Keep playing the main story and exploring its odd corners; when the moment happens, the trophy is yours.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade
trophies.guide: Bowl people over with a melee drive-by — hit them with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. The name is a bowling joke, and the trophy is hidden, so it is most likely tied to a story moment at or after the bowling alley. In free roam, the technique is the same: drive slowly past a group, swing a melee weapon from the vehicle, and knock them down. If it does not pop in free roam, it is waiting in the story.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target ($250,000)
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists — take them to your contacts, who launder them into clean cash for a cut. Keep robbing and laundering through the game and the total will climb; the trophy pops at $250,000 earned this way. It pairs naturally with the bank vault and shop robberies.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target ($100,000)
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every dollar you spend in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, ammo, food and cars all add to the total. Do not save this one for last: spend normally as you play, buy the gear you need, and the total will reach $100,000 on its own. If you are short at the end, buy expensive ammo or a vehicle to top it up.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (8)
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are the properties you buy to store vehicles — find all 8 for sale around Leonida and buy each one. They cost money, so save up through the story and the laundering for Dime on the Dollar, then buy the garages in one sweep. Owning them also gives you somewhere to keep the 100 vehicles for Whip It Good.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
PSNProfiles — grade and PSN progress target (10)
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-game vehicle service — open the app, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until you have 10 registered. Use a mix of cars and bikes you already own so you do not have to buy new ones just for this trophy. The count is tracked by PlayStation.
